questions.question: If 19 July 2000 was a Wednesday, then what would be the day of the week on 15 June 2012?
questions.solution:
Odd days:

A non-leap year has 365 days and a leap year has 366 days.

**Non-leap year =** 365 days or 52 weeks and 1 day. So, here the number of odd days is 1.

**Leap year =** 366 days or 52 weeks and 2 days So, here the number of odd days are 2.

Leap year between 2000 to 2012 = 2004, 2008 and 2012

And,

The non-leap year between 2000 and 2012 = 2001, 2002, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010 and 2011

So, total number of odd day between 2000 and 2012 = 9 (Total Non- leap year) + 2 + 2 + 2 = 15 days = 1 odd day

 
 

 
 
**Code of the day**

 
 
 
**Day**

 
 
 

 
 
0

 
 
 
Sunday

 
 
 

 
 
1

 
 
 
Monday

 
 
 

 
 
2

 
 
 
Tuesday

 
 
 

 
 
3

 
 
 
Wednesday

 
 
 

 
 
4

 
 
 
Thursday

 
 
 

 
 
5

 
 
 
Friday

 
 
 

 
 
6

 
 
 
Saturday

 
 
 

 

**19 July 2000 was a Wednesday**

=> Day on 19 July 2012 = Wednesday + 15

= Wednesday + remainder of 15/7

= Wednesday + 1 (odd day) = Thursday

**Therefore, 19 July 2012 = Thursday**

Now,

**15 June 2012 = 19 July 2012 – 34 days**

= Thursday – 34

= Thursday – the remainder of 34/7

= Thursday – 6 (In reverse direction)

= Friday

Hence, 15 June 2012 was **“Friday”.**

questions.question: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-pair that is different.
questions.solution:
The logic is here is:

**(1st number)² × 2 = 2ⁿd number**

**Option (1): **12 : 288

Now, follow the logic:

(12)² × 2

= 144 × 2 = 288 = 2ⁿd number

This option follows the pattern.

**Option (2):** 14 : 392

Now, follow the logic:

(14)² × 2

= 196 × 2 = 392 = 2ⁿd number

This option follows the pattern.

**Option (3):** 19 : 622

**Now, follow the logic:**

**(19)² × 2 **

**= 361 × 2 = 722 ****≠**** 2ⁿd number **

**This option do not follow the pattern.**

**Option (4):** 11 : 242

Now, follow the logic:

(11)² × 2

= 121 × 2 = 242 = 2ⁿd number

This option follows the pattern.

Hence, pair **“****19 : 622”** is an odd one.

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(44, 24, 132)
questions.solution:
The Logic here is as follows:

**(1st Number × 2ⁿd number) ÷ 8 = 3rd Number**

**In **(44, 24, 132)

(1st Number × 2ⁿd number) ÷ 8 = 3rd Number

(44 × 24) ÷ 8

= 1056 ÷ 8 = 132 = 3rd Number

Now check the all options,

**Option (1) **(46, 22, 306)

(1st Number × 2ⁿd number) ÷ 8 = 3rd Number

(46 × 22) ÷ 8

= 1012 ÷ 8 = 126.5 ≠ 3rd Number

**Option (2) **(32, 28, 250)

(1st Number × 2ⁿd number) ÷ 8 = 3rd Number

(32 × 28) ÷ 8

= 896 ÷ 8 = 112 ≠ 3rd Number

**Option (3) **(16, 26, 186)

(1st Number × 2ⁿd number) ÷ 8 = 3rd Number

(16 × 26) ÷ 8

= 416 ÷ 8 = 52 ≠ 3rd Number

**Option (4) (56, 26, 182)**

**(1st Number × 2ⁿd number) ÷ 8 = 3rd Number**

**(56 × 26) ÷ 8 **

**= 1456 ÷ 8 = 182 = 3rd Number**

Hence, the correct answer is **"****(56, 26, 182)****".**

questions.question:
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series.

J P _ L D _ P _ M D J _ C _ D _ P C _ D

options.text: C, J, C, P, O, J, P
C, J, C, P, N, P, O
C, J, N, P, O, J, O
C, J, C, P, N, J, O

questions.solution:
We put all the option in blank area and check who create particular pattern

**1) ****C, J, C, P, O, J, P**

J P _ L D _ P _ M D J _ C _ D _ P C _ D

After filling the blanks with the letters/numbers in the option given above, we get:

J P **__C__** L D / **__J__** P **__C__** M D / J **__P__** C **__O__** D / **__J__** P C **__P__** D

No particular pattern is repeating itself when the sequence is divided into equal parts.

**2) ****C, J, C, P, N, P, O**

J P _ L D _ P _ M D J _ C _ D _ P C _ D

After filling the blanks with the letters/numbers in the option given above, we get:

J P **__C__** L D / **__J__** P **__C__** M D / J **__P__** C **__N__** D / **__P__** P C **__O__** D

No particular pattern is repeating itself when the sequence is divided into equal parts.

**3) ****C, J, N, P, O, J, O**

J P _ L D _ P _ M D J _ C _ D _ P C _ D

After filling the blanks with the letters/numbers in the option given above, we get:

J P **__C__** L D / **__J__** P **__N__** M D / J **__P__** C **__O__** D / **__J__** P C **__O__** D

No particular pattern is repeating itself when the sequence is divided into equal parts.

**4) ****C, J, C, P, N, J, O**

**J P _ L D _ P _ M D J _ C _ D _ P C _ D**

**After filling the blanks with the letters/numbers in the option given above, we get:**

J P **__C__** L D / **__J__** P **__C__** M D / J **__P__** C **__N__** D / **__J__** P C **__O__** D

**Here fourth letter of word is increasing by +1.**

**L + 1 = M, M + 1 = N, N + 1 = O**

**A particular pattern is repeating itself when the sequence is divided into equal parts.**

Hence, ‘**C, J, C, P, N, J, O**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:

‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’.

‘A & B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’.

‘A % B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’.

If ‘W # Q @ T & Y @ M % K’, then how is K related to T?
questions.solution:
‘A # B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’.

‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’.

‘A & B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’.

‘A % B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’.

Let us first decode the given symbols and then draw a family tree.

 
 

 
 
**A is**

 
 
 

 
 
**Symbol**

 
 
 
#

 
 
 
@

 
 
 
&

 
 
 
%

 
 
 

 
 
**Meaning**

 
 
 
Brother

 
 
 
Daughter

 
 
 
Husband

 
 
 
Wife

 
 
 

 
 
**to B**

 
 
 

 

Now break the code of ‘W # Q @ T & Y @ M % K’

**1) ****W # Q**

‘W # Q’ means ‘W is the brother of Q’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a7ac5f5efce6890c50d953553c2cec1d390b6f85fb8d0907493665d0eda9397.png]

**3) ****T & Y**

‘T & Y’ means ‘T is the husband of Y’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc56ba6ecf01752c46962689100499e7d35f9c2f7c58871d08f6d3f26d680990.png] 

**4) ****Y @ M**

‘Y @ M’ means ‘Y is the daughter of M’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7dfe0c74265414c150ec8cdf3fb33de027472d7fac796137e85fafebe585e2e6.png] 

**5) M % K**

‘M % K’ means ‘M is the wife of K’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e8161111c9ef78fc5e3d64dc90587540ec0f1586e28f6e0b12628fdee15f3d5.png] 

Hence, K is the **“Father-in-law” **of T.
